rv.q: The four young Liverpudlians who make up Rain are such dead ringers for the original Beatles that watching them is like peering through a time machine.
Although purists might sneer at this concert/theatrical experience, there’s no denying that, as cover bands go, this is one of the best.
But after a show like this, the only impression that is left are those classic songs. And that's as it should be.
It hits all the right notes, but an imitation is still an imitation.
This Beatles tribute show is a slick, shriekingly loud and numbingly faithful reproduction of the Fab Four's musical evolution.
Primarily, however, 'Rain' is a Vegas act for All Hallow's Eve -- a rock horror show.
The homage often feels tired and cheesy, and audience members unwilling to frequently stand up and clap along may be uncomfortable.
They're quite polished at what they do, which is to ape the Beatles' every intonation and gesture.
Rain may not be theatre but it sure is entertaining.
Your affinity for the Fab Four, cover-band mimicry and bad mop-top wigs will be a good gauge for whether or not this nonstop nostalgia trip is for you.
Rain is either a new low point or a refreshingly honest enterprise.
